reasoning_content:
The "V-only" rule (optimized relative vessel density mean > 48.97) exactly reproduces sensitivity 81.82%, specificity 90.91%, accuracy 86.36% — matches the published values perfectly! Also, the OR rule gives the same accuracy but with sensitivity/specificity swapped. The min-score with the best cutoff also gives 86.36% accuracy with sensitivity 81.82 / specificity 90.91.

The V-only rule matches all three published metrics (sensitivity 81.82, specificity 90.91, accuracy 86.36). This strongly suggests that the paper's classification was effectively driven by the vessel density cutoff (or that the "match" rule was vessel-density-based). In fact, the min-score with optimized cutoff 48.97... the best min cutoff found is 48.15, not 48.97. But V-only at 48.97 gives exactly sensitivity=81.82, specificity=90.91, accuracy=86.36.

Hmm, but is V-only justifiable? The paper states "a match was defined when the relative vessel density and tumoroid diameter in the on-chip model were consistent with the patient's clinical outcome." Ambiguous. But our reconstruction: predicted resistant if optimized relative vessel density (mean of 3 bevacizumab doses) > 48.97 (published optimized cutoff). This exactly reproduces all three published metrics.

Alternatively, the OR rule also gives accuracy 86.36 but with sensitivity 90.91 / specificity 81.82 (swapped), which does not match the published sensitivity/specificity. Therefore V-only is the consistent reconstruction.

But wait: maybe the paper used a different aggregation (e.g., only the 1 µM dose?). Let's check: V at 1 µM optimized > 48.97? Values: P01 49.72 yes... Let me quickly test other aggregations to see which one exactly reproduces sensitivity 81.82 / specificity 90.91. V-only mean already matches. Good.

Also check the truth assignment: 11 resistant / 11 sensitive. Sensitivity = TP/11 = 9/11? Wait, V-only: predicted n=10; TP = 9? Let me recompute: sensitivity 0.8182 = 9/11, specificity 0.9091 = 10/11, accuracy = 19/22 = 0.8636. Yes.

Therefore records: 22 patients, score = mean of optimized relative vessel density across 3 bevacizumab concentrations (refs E, F, G columns of sheet 5n), threshold 48.97, op ">" → predicted resistant (positive). Truth: resistant = 1 for the 11 patients read from Figure 5P (vision reference), sensitive = 0.

Our score is relative vessel density (vessel) — but the paper's match uses both vessel and tumoroid. The reconstruction that matches exactly uses vessel density only...
